observed.facings.png: Three facings shown at one scale. They are close in height, and each one is the same lean, crested raptor with grey-brown plumage. The feathers have glowing orange-yellow edges, and the long tail plumes end in flame-like tips. Every facing perches on a charred stick whose far end is burning with a small open flame.
observed.south.png: Front view. The bird faces the camera with two amber eyes and a hooked beak pointing down at the viewer, and a spiky orange-tipped crest. The wings are folded at the sides with glowing orange edges, and the chest is grey-brown with orange streaks. The tail plumes sweep off to the lower left with flame-coloured tips. The talons grip a charred twig that is burning at its right end. Clean alpha, with no ground patch.
observed.east.png: True side profile facing right. The hooked beak, amber eye and swept-back crest are visible. The wings are folded along the back, layered with feathers that have ember-orange edges. The tail is long and trails to the lower left as flame-tipped plumes. The legs are long and thin, and the talons grip a twig burning at its front end. The silhouette is lean and long-legged, reading like a secretary bird or a slim hawk. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: Rear view. It shows the back of the head and crest, the folded wings meeting down the back, and a long tail hanging straight down with flaming tips. At most the head turns slightly right, with a faint hint of the beak edge. No eye is clearly visible, and the face is not presented. The burning end of the twig shows at the viewer's left, which matches the bird's left side as seen in the south view. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the bird is a little over one cell long, smaller than the human but large for a raptor, which fits drawSize 1.1. At 32 px per cell it reads as a dark grey bird shape with an orange tail and a tiny flame accent, clearly apart from the ground.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the face head-on: both eyes, the beak toward the camera, and the chest.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the back of the head, the folded wings and the hanging tail. No eyes are clearly visible, with at most a faint hint of the beak from a slight head turn.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three facings are standing views from the game's angled camera. None is a top-down view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: Code measured a 6% height spread, and the facings look visually consistent.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: Every facing has the same crest, palette, ember-edged wings, flame tail and burning twig. The twig's burning end stays on the bird's left side across views.

SIGNATURE.seen: The burning twig with a visible flame is held in the talons on every facing, and the ember-glow plumage reads as a fire bird.

ALIEN.seen: The head and body are hawk-like, but the glowing ember-edged feathers, flame-tipped tail plumes and burning twig stop it reading as a plain Earth hawk.

DEPARTURES.seen: 1) The body is mostly grey with warm brown undertones and is not barred. It reads as ash/soot-grey, though a bit warm on the south chest. 2) The ember-orange markings glow along the feather edges and do not read as flat russet. 3) A burning twig with a visible flame is held in the talons on all facings. 4) The silhouette is lean and long-legged, slimmer than a stocky hawk.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px per cell it reads as a dark bird shape with an orange tail and a flame accent.

subject: RM_FireWasp

reply.subject: RM_FireWasp

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. All three show the same insect: a body covered in overlapping brown, pinecone-like plates with orange glowing seams between them, broad tattered wings that look like dry leaves with brown veins, thin jointed legs, and orange flames licking up around the body and wing bases. South and north show the wings spread to both sides. East shows a side profile with both wings raised up and back. East looks a little taller because the wings are raised.
observed.south.png: Front view. The head faces the camera: two dark compound eyes, mandibles and short antennae, with a plated thorax behind it. The wings are spread symmetrically left and right, with flames rising behind the shoulders. The plated abdomen is mostly hidden behind the head. Legs hang below. Clean transparent background.
observed.east.png: True side profile facing right. Head with a dark eye and long curved antennae, a plated thorax, a narrow wasp waist and a large drooping abdomen made of pinecone-like overlapping scales with glowing seams. Six thin jointed legs. Two broad, torn, leaf-like wings angled up and back. Flame wisps run along the back and around the abdomen.
observed.north.png: Rear view. A tapering plated abdomen points toward the camera, with layered scales like a pinecone and orange glow between them. Two antenna tips show above the body. No eyes and no face. The wings are spread symmetrically, flames sit at the wing roots, and the legs splay out to the sides.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the wasp is about 1.5 cells long, roughly as tall as the vanilla human and much bigger than the rat. At 32 px per cell it still reads as an orange, flame-edged winged insect, clearly apart from the ground.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the head head-on, with both eyes and the mandibles toward the camera.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the tapering plated abdomen tip. Only antenna tips show above it; there are no eyes and no face.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three are angled camera views: legs hang below the body and the body has depth. None is a flat dorsal view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The 17% spread comes from east's wings being raised high above the body. Body length and bulk match across facings, so this is a pose, not a size jump.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The same pinecone plating, glowing seams, leaf-like torn wings, legs and flames appear on every facing. The wings turn with the body: spread sideways on south and north, raised in profile on east.

SIGNATURE.seen: The fire-proof plating and the flames around the insect are both prominent.

ALIEN.seen: The silhouette is wasp-like, with a waist and antennae, but the heavy pinecone plating, leaf-membrane wings and flames make it read as an invented fire insect, not a recoloured wasp.

DEPARTURES.seen: 1 PRESENT: the whole body is overlapping heavy scales. 2 PRESENT: there are no yellow-and-black stripes; the colour is brown plates with orange seams. 3 PRESENT: broad wings are held spread, with no motion blur. 4 MOSTLY PRESENT: it is drawn inside flames, but the orange glow between the plates makes the scales look a little like smouldering embers rather than untouched by fire.

STYLE.seen: Painterly, detailed, realistic texture with no cute face, no cel shading and no 3D-render look.

OURS.seen: A bespoke generated design. It is not a vanilla or other-mod insect.

ALPHA.seen: Clean cut-out. The only soft, semi-transparent pixels are the flames, which the description asks for. There is no ground patch or shadow.

SCALE.seen: About as tall as a human at drawSize 2. The description gives no size words; 'barely a threat to a grown person' allows a large insect, though it is on the big side for a swarm insect.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px per cell it reads as an orange-edged winged insect with a clear silhouette.

WINGS_FOLDED.seen: The grounded sprite has its wings spread on every facing. The card's departure 3 requires the wings held spread for gliding, so this is intended. The owner also kept a flyer with raised wings before.

findings.seen: Wings spread wide or raised on every facing of the grounded sprite.
findings.quote: Grounded: wings folded and symmetric (raised wings are polish — the owner kept one).
findings.fix: Keep the wings spread and symmetric as departure 3 requires; spread wings are the intended resting pose for this glider.

findings.quote: drawn hanging inside flames or heat-haze with its scales untouched by fire
findings.fix: The scale plates stay cool and unburnt in tone, with flames and heat-haze wrapping around the insect but no ember glow inside the plating.

findings.quote: Scale beside the human against the description's size words
findings.fix: The fire wasp stands about half to two-thirds of a human's height, so a swarm of several fits over a burn.
